item.title: Water into fuel: The new nanomaterial that could upgrade green hydrogen
item.description: Generating hydrogen without releasing carbon dioxide sounds simple: pass electricity through water, split water molecules and generate green hydrogen. item.title: Silent bacterial genes yield potential leads for future cancer drugs
item.description: Natural products produced by microorganisms are a promising source of new drugs. Researchers at the Helmholtz Center for Infection Research (HZI) and its Saarbrücken-based site, the Helmholtz Institute for Pharmaceutical Research Saarland (HIPS), have now discovered a new family of such compounds, elucidated their unusual biosynthesis and developed a way to produce them synthetically. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can cats really thrive on vegan diets? Professor Andrew Knight responds to critics
item.description: In response to a recent article on vegan diets for cats, Phys.org received numerous messages from concerned readers. People raised a lot of concerns, mainly arguing that cats are obligate carnivores and that vegan diets could be very harmful to their health. Now, we have collected all these comments, questions and concerns and asked the researcher behind the original paper to address them. Andrew Knight, Veterinary Professor of Animal Welfare and Associate Professor at Murdoch University School of Veterinary Medicine, offers his response below. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Cuando la sonda OSIRIS-REx, de la NASA, llegó a su destino en el asteroide Bennu en 2018, se encontró con algo inesperado. Según las mediciones tomadas por el telescopio Spitzer en 2007, este asteroide se calienta mucho cuando está expuesto a la radiación solar y se enfría igual de rápido por la noche. Esto es algo que en la Tierra ocurre en zonas que están cubiertas por roca fina, como la arena de playa. Por eso, pensaron que tocar la superficie y tomar muestras sería coser y cantar. item.description: DNA-nano/microparticle motors are among the fastest artificial molecular motors reported to date, moving at approximately 30 nm per second. item.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
item.description: Abstract: "Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. item.title: Hidden chromosome structures reveal greater complexity in how roundworms organize DNA
item.description: Almost every cell in our body contains around two meters (6.6 feet) of DNA, packed into a tiny nucleus. Yet for the cell to function, this enormous amount of genetic material must remain organized and accessible. Researchers at the University of Basel have now discovered three distinct types of large chromosomal domains that help organize DNA in nuclei. Fuente: Phys.org.
